chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, similar to it. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, from one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), I guess it was Abu Aasim al-Sijistani.

He said: 'I was a fellow traveller of Abdullah ibn al-Najjashy, and he held the opinion of the Zaydiyya. So when we were in Medina, he went to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). So when he returned, I saw him gloomy. So when it was morning, he said to me, 'Get me permission to see Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).' So I went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said, 'Abdullah ibn al-Najjashy, who holds the opinion of the Zaydiyya, and he had gone to Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and he asked me to seek permission for him from you.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Give him permission.'

So he entered upon him and greeted, saying, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! I am a man who befriends you, and I say that the truth is with you, and I have killed seven from those whom I heard insulting the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So I asked about that Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and he said to me, 'You are liable for their blood in the world and the Hereafter.' So I said, 'So why do the people antagonise me when I am liable for the blood of the one I hear insulting Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)?'

So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'So how did you kill them?' He said, 'Among them was one whom the road gathered between me and him, so I killed him. And among them was one whose house I entered, so I killed him, and that was concealed from me, all of it.'

So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O Abu Khidash! Upon you, for each man from them whom you killed, is a ram that you slaughter in Mina, because you killed them without the permission of the Imam. And if you had killed them with the permission of the Imam, there would not be upon you anything in the world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِ الْإِمَامِ: Without the permission of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing someone who insults the Imams without the Imam's direct permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinction between personal vengeance and juridical authority in Shia fiqh, where Imam al-Sadiq (as) clarifies that killing insulter without the Imam's explicit permission incurs a sacrificial expiation (kaffarah), akin to slaughtering a ram at Mina. It underscores the Zaydi context of Abdullah ibn al-Najjashy, showing that even those who acknowledged the Ahl al-Bayt's right to leadership were subject to the Imam's specific legal rulings on blood money and retribution. This narrative reinforces the principle of 'qatl bi ghayr idhn al-imam' as a key mechanism for maintaining order and preventing arbitrary violence in the community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibn Mahboub – similar to it. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, raising it, (It has been narrated) from one of the companions of Abu Abdullahasws, I guess it was Abu Aasim Al-Sajistany

who said, ‘I was a fellow traveller of Abdullah Bin Al-Najjashy, and he viewed by the opinion of Al-Zaydiyya. So when we were at Al-Medina, he went to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan (Al Basry), and I went to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So when I left, I saw him gloomy. So when it was the morning he said to me, ‘Get me permission to (see) Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and said, ‘Abdullah Bin Al-Najjashy, who views by the opinions of Al-Zaydiyya, and he had gone to Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan, and has asked me that I seek permission for him, to (see) you<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘Give permission to him’.

So he came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said, ‘O son<sup>asws</sup> of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I am a man who has befriended you<sup>asws</sup>, and I am saying that the truth is among you<sup>asws</sup>, and I have killed seven from the ones whom I heard insulting Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>. So I asked Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan about that, so he said to me, ‘You will be seized for their blood in the world and the Hereafter’. So I said, ‘So why do the people antagonise me when I am to be seized with the blood of the one I hear insulting Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>?’

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘So how did you kill them?’ He said, ‘Among them was one whom there was a gathering between me and him, on the road, so I killed him. And among them was one whom I went over to, in his house, so I killed him, and that is concealed (matter) upon me, all of it’.

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘O Abu Jidash! It is upon you, with each man you killed from them, a ram. You should slaughter it at Mina, because you killed them without permission from the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. And had you kill them with the permission of the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, there would not happen to be upon you anything in the world and the Hereafter’.
